title: Adiabaticity for the two-level system
lead: A two-level system whose detuning and Rabi frequency change in time: its time-dependent dressed states and mixing angle, adiabatic return and rapid adiabatic passage, the condition under which the system follows its instantaneous ground state, and the exactly solvable Landau-Zener model of a linear sweep through resonance.
exercise_notes: The section prints no invitation, and no MIT 8.422 problem maps to Chapter 7.

figures.original_caption: A comparison of adiabatic passage and adiabatic return. The time dependent parameters Δ and Ω lead to instantaneous eigenenergies ϵ±. Assuming that the system follows the instantaneous ground state, it will be in a mixture of states |1⟩ and |2⟩ with occupation probabilities P₁ and P₂ respectively. Clearly, adiabatic passage can result in state transfer, whereas adiabatic return leaves the system in its initial state.

footnotes.html: The book cites Fig. (9.3) and leaves the parenthesis open. The figure meant is Figure 7.1.

The ratio that runs from near $-\infty$ to near $\infty$ is $\kDelta/\kOmega$. As $\kDelta$ is swept through resonance, $\kOmega/\kDelta$ passes from near 0 through $\pm\infty$ and back to near 0, while $\tan 2\ktheta = -2\kOmega/\kDelta$ turns the mixing angle by $\pi/2$.
As printed, $\epsilon$ has the dimension of an inverse action. The dimensionless ratio that Eq. (7.19) compares with one is $\epsilon = \hbar\dot{\ktheta}/|\kepsp - \kepsm|$.

With $\kDelta = \kalpha\kt$ and $\kOmega = \kOmega_0$, Eq. (7.16) gives $\dot{\ktheta} = \kalpha\kOmega_0/(\kalpha^2\kt^2 + 4\kOmega_0^2)$, which at resonance is $\kalpha/4\kOmega_0$, not $\kalpha/2\kOmega_0$. With the splitting $2\hbar\kOmega_0$ the small parameter is $\epsilon \approx \kalpha/8\kOmega_0^2$.

$\kPLZ - 1$ is negative. The non-adiabatic correction is $1 - \kPLZ = e^{-2\pi|\kOmega_0|^2/|\kalpha|}$, exactly, by Eq. (7.22). In terms of $\epsilon$ it is $e^{-\pi/2\epsilon}$ with the book's $\epsilon \approx \kalpha/4\kOmega_0^2$, and $e^{-\pi/4\epsilon}$ with $\epsilon \approx \kalpha/8\kOmega_0^2$.

In the book's Adiabatic Passage panel the curve that starts at 1 is labelled $P_2$ and the curve that rises to 1 is labelled $P_1$. For the transfer from $|1\rangle$ to $|2\rangle$ that the caption and the text describe, the falling curve is $\kPone$ and the rising one $\kPtwo$, as the Adiabatic Return panel's colours have them.

nodes.note: The book prints $\langle\dot{+}|-\rangle = \dot{\ktheta}(\kt)$; differentiating (7.13) and projecting on (7.14) gives $-\dot{\ktheta}(\kt)$. Only the magnitude enters (7.19).

steps.cap: For the two dressed states, $k = +$ and $l = -$.
$\langle -|\dot{+}\rangle$ is the complex conjugate of $\langle\dot{+}|-\rangle$, which is real.
Multiplying through by the splitting; in a sweep the mixing angle turns one way, so $|\dot{\theta}| = \dot{\theta}$.

assumes.text: The energy difference is smallest when $\kDelta$ sweeps through resonance: $\kepsp(\kt) - \kepsm(\kt) \geq 2\hbar\kOmega(\kt)$.

Integrating over the whole pulse; the right side is the pulse area $A$.
